title: Your NRI Streaming Guide: 'Mismatched' Ends, 'Madhuvidhu' Debuts, and a Court Battle Almost Killed 'Dhurandhar'
excerpt: What to watch this week on Netflix, SonyLIV, and Sun NXT — plus the copyright fight that nearly pulled a Ranveer Singh film off digital shelves.
body:
If you're an NRI scrolling through streaming apps wondering what to watch this week, here's your guide — from an emotional farewell on Netflix to a legal battle that almost killed an OTT premiere.

'Mismatched' Says Goodbye After Seven Years

Prajakta Koli is crying. Not dramatically, not for content — genuinely crying, because the woman who built a YouTube empire as MostlySane is about to say goodbye to Dimple Ahuja, the character she's played across four seasons of Netflix India's Mismatched.

"I have been Dimple for almost seven years now," Koli told interviewers, her voice catching. "I am dreading each day because I know the end is coming."

The final season of Mismatched — based on Sandhya Menon's novel When Dimple Met Rishi — will resolve the long-simmering romance between Dimple and Rishi (Rohit Saraf) that has made the show a comfort watch for young Indians and NRIs alike. The show's appeal was always its specificity: the arranged-marriage tension, the Ahmedabad setting, the very Indian way two people can like each other and still not say it for three seasons.

For diaspora viewers who found Mismatched during the pandemic and kept returning, the final season is appointment television. Koli has teased "second chances and emotional reinvention" — exactly the themes that hit different when you're 8,000 miles from home.

Available on Netflix worldwide.

'Madhuvidhu' — A Malayalam Rom-Com Lands on SonyLIV

If you need something lighter after the Mismatched emotions, Madhuvidhu arrives on SonyLIV on May 22. The Malayalam romantic comedy stars Sharafudheen and Kalyani Panicker in a newlywed story that early reviews describe as "warm, funny, and refreshingly low-stakes."

Malayalam cinema's OTT game has been quietly excellent — from The Great Indian Kitchen to Kumbalangi Nights to Manjummel Boys, the industry consistently delivers films that NRIs recommend to their non-Indian friends. Madhuvidhu looks poised to join that list.

Streaming May 22 on SonyLIV. Available internationally.

'Kaalidas 2' — Tamil Noir on Sun NXT

For those who prefer their entertainment with a body count, Kaalidas 2 is now streaming on Sun NXT. The Tamil crime thriller stars Bharath in a sequel to the 2019 original, which earned a cult following for its tight plotting and moody cinematography.

The sequel reportedly ups the stakes with a darker narrative and more complex character work. Tamil crime thrillers have carved a dedicated niche on OTT platforms, and Kaalidas 2 arrives at a time when NRI audiences are actively seeking alternatives to the formulaic Bollywood fare that dominates most streaming libraries.

Now streaming on Sun NXT.

'Dhurandhar' Survives a Copyright Battle

The most dramatic streaming story this week happened in a courtroom. The Delhi High Court refused to stay the OTT release of Dhurandhar: The Revenge, a film that faced a copyright infringement claim from the makers of Tirchi Topiwale. T-Series, the film's distributor, successfully argued that the similarities were superficial.

The case highlights a growing trend in Indian entertainment: as OTT platforms multiply and content libraries expand, copyright disputes are becoming the new battleground. For viewers, the ruling means Dhurandhar — Ranveer Singh's latest — remains available for streaming.

What Else to Know

The OTT landscape for Indian content has never been richer, and NRIs are its most valuable audience. Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney+ Hotstar, SonyLIV, JioCinema, and Sun NXT all carry substantial Indian libraries, but discovery remains a challenge. The days of waiting months for a theatrical release to hit streaming are over — most major Indian films now arrive on OTT within 4-6 weeks of theatrical release, and some premieres are OTT-first.

The advice? Keep SonyLIV and Sun NXT on your radar alongside the bigger platforms. The best Indian content right now isn't always where you'd expect it.
